summary: Firmed up a boundary of the trim finding and dispatched its measurement. The account claimed snapshot-based compaction remains available under the same configuration, but only from source; I added a snapshot call to every case of the trim probe after the two trim calls and validated it locally — for {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} and the two-node {1,3} the snapshot returns ok and moves the compacted index 0→1 exactly where trim cannot, while in the contiguous control it is a no-op because trim already compacted that index — and submitted the extended probe with three boundary comparisons (applicable only where the trim path left the compacted index at 0). I also read the entry-deriving macro crate and found no lead there. Incomplete: that receipt is pending; both established findings (the actor layer's false `Ok` completion for a lost entry, bounded to tick periods above the re-synchronisation round trip and relied on by the repository's own async example, and the core's trim path being unable to compact whenever the largest node id exceeds the node count) rest on complete comparison chains with nothing outstanding beyond same-cause variants.
